date_fields.registry_as_of: When the registry's sources were last checked for that version.
date_fields.retrieved: When the registry retrieved the source.
date_fields.source_published: The source's own publication date (null if the source states none).

description: Changes to TheMoroccoAI's documented record between published registry versions, classified by what changed. They describe the record, not events in the world.
limitations: Changes describe the registry's record between published versions, not events in the world: a record admitted in a version documents something that may have happened much earlier.

Dates are kept apart: source_published is the source's own date, retrieved is when the registry retrieved it, and registry_as_of is when the version's sources were last checked. No event date is inferred.
A text revision is 'editorial' only if it differs in whitespace, case or punctuation; otherwise its effect on the finding is 'undetermined' and is read from the before and after texts.
Snapshots are the published versions on the repository's main history; changes made between versions are not seen separately.
Source disappearance or modification is not detected here: tools/check_sources.py re-checks sources, and only a recorded correction appears as a change.

materiality.structural: Format, schema or bookkeeping; no finding changed.
materiality.undetermined: A wording revision whose effect on the finding is not judged automatically.

fields.after: Open-access article (CC BY 4.0), published online 3 October 2025. Every author lists an affiliation with the university that hosts and runs Toubkal, so the workload statement is the operator's own report, peer-reviewed but not independent. It documents specific fine-tuning runs, not the scale, share or continuity of AI use. The article names their authors "Belkasmi et al.", but its reference [57] is the GemMaroc preprint by Skiredj, Azhari, Atou, Tazi and Berrada (MAI-EV-0042); that preprint does not itself say where the runs were made. The article's statement that they ran on Toubkal comes from its own authors, none of whom is an author of the preprint. The article's user counts and utilisation figures are not recorded. Benchmark, accuracy and energy figures in the article are not recorded. The verified fact is what the article states. after.text: Toubkal is listed in the June 2026 TOP500 as general-purpose high-performance computing; the listing documents capacity, not workloads or users.

A peer-reviewed article by authors affiliated with its host university states that large-language-model fine-tuning has been run on it, and presents as a benchmark the runs that produced the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija models.

The GemMaroc preprint that the article cites (Skiredj et al.; three of its five authors are from the host university) reports the hardware used, A100 GPUs and, for its largest model, eight H100 GPUs, and about 48 GPU-hours for that longest run, but does not say where the runs were made, and expresses their cost at a commercial cloud provider's public rate.
Two researchers of the host university report training a bacterial genomic language model on Toubkal: two A100 GPUs for 37 hours.

Its official 2030 objectives include 240,000 direct jobs with a contribution to GDP, digitalised public services, and a rise from 113th to 50th place in the e-government development index.

after.text: The strategy was launched in Rabat on 25 September 2024 by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform.

Its official 2030 objectives include 240,000 direct jobs with a contribution to GDP, digitalised public services, and a rise from 113th to 50th place worldwide on the ranking of online public services. The strategy's brochure defines that ranking as the United Nations Online Services Index (OSI), a component of the e-government development index (EGDI), and gives 113th as Morocco's 2022 position on it; the national news agency's dispatch calls it the e-government development index.

The Head of Government stated that public investment in digital technology rose from MAD 11 million in 2021 to more than MAD 1.7 billion in 2024. The registry has not checked these figures or matched them to any budget execution figure, and spending is an input, not a measure of the targets.
The ministry's report on the First National AI Conference frames the conference within the strategy.

On the overall e-government development index, the United Nations ranked Morocco 101st in 2022 and 90th in 2024. On the Online Services Index, its page gives Morocco's value (0.47210 in 2022, 0.56184 in 2024) but not its rank, so the strategy's 113th place for 2022 is the strategy's figure and has not been verified against a United Nations ranking. The 2024 edition, published in the year of the launch, measures the starting position, not progress under the strategy.

Before the launch, the ministry's finance-law performance projects set other targets for its digital-transition programme: an overall EGDI rank of 75th by 2026 in the 2023 bill, then 85th by 2026 in the 2024 bill, against a 2022 value of 101; and jobs created of 190,000 by 2030 in the 2023 bill, then 270,000 by 2030 in the 2024 bill, defined as digital-economy jobs on formal contracts, whose 2022 value of 130,000 covers offshoring only. These are programme targets, not the strategy's, and the registry does not reconcile them with the strategy's 240,000 direct jobs or its Online Services Index objective.

The 2026 finance law provides MAD 1,500,000,000 in payment appropriations for implementing the strategy. That is an authorisation to spend, not expenditure: no amount committed, disbursed or spent is recorded in this registry.

The ministry reports more than 148,500 jobs in the offshoring sector at the end of 2024, and 22,649 new enrolments in digital training in 2024–2025 against 21,125 the year before. These are unverified ministry-reported outputs on definitions that differ from the strategy's objectives: offshoring jobs are not total digital jobs, and enrolments are neither graduates nor certified talents.

The Cour des comptes reported 605 digitalised public services at the end of 2023, of which no more than 23 per cent were completely digitalised. This independent audit finding describes the position before the strategy's launch, not progress under it.

Before the launch, the ministry's finance-law performance projects set other targets for its digital-transition programme: an overall EGDI rank of 75th by 2026 in the 2023 bill, then 85th by 2026 in the 2024 bill, against a 2022 value of 101; and jobs created of 190,000 by 2030 in the 2023 bill, then 270,000 by 2030 in the 2024 bill, defined as digital-economy jobs on formal contracts, whose 2022 value of 130,000 covers offshoring only. These are programme targets, not the strategy's, and the registry does not reconcile them with the strategy's 240,000 direct jobs or its Online Services Index objective.

A 2025 ministry report presents a circular on the offshoring sector with objectives of 270,000 direct jobs by 2030, from 130,000 in 2022. It attributes that figure to the offshoring sector; it does not state how the figure relates to the strategy's direct-jobs objective or to the earlier finance-law targets, and the registry does not reconcile them.

The 2025 and 2026 finance laws each provide MAD 1,500,000,000 in payment appropriations for implementing the strategy, under project 20 of programme 429, a code that designated a different line in the 2024 finance law. Each is an authorisation to spend in its own year, not expenditure, and the two are not added together: no amount committed, disbursed or spent on the strategy is recorded in this registry. Budget execution is published only as ministry-level totals, which are recorded for the ministry, not for the strategy.

The ministry reports more than 148,500 jobs in the offshoring sector at the end of 2024, and 22,649 new enrolments in digital training in 2024–2025 against 21,125 the year before. These are unverified ministry-reported outputs on definitions that differ from the strategy's objectives: offshoring jobs are not total digital jobs, and enrolments are neither graduates nor certified talents.

The Cour des comptes reported 605 digitalised public services at the end of 2023, of which no more than 23 per cent were completely digitalised. This independent audit finding describes the position before the strategy's launch, not progress under it.
